parts.title: A Frog, a Bird and a Fish: One Group or THREE? (Part 1) | Animal Groups
parts.description:
A frog, a bird and a fish, all at one pond in Sungei Buloh. Are they one group of animals, or three? Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity: animal groups (amphibians, birds and fish).

In this part:
• What an animal is: a head, a body and limbs
• Outer coverings and observable characteristics
• Be the frog: on land, then under water
• Amphibians: moist skin, land and water, eggs in water

Key words: outer covering, observable characteristics, amphibians, moist skin.
Watch Part 2 to meet the fish that hops on land!

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies! Practise this topic in TheOneApp.

Singapore Primary 3 Science (2023 syllabus): Diversity, classification of living things: animals, amphibians, birds and fish (Chapter 2, pp. 23–28). Also fits US NGSS 4-LS1-1 (Grade 3 to 4).
Try it for real (School Lab 2.1B, Coat and cover): feel a fallen feather and a fish scale from the market. Which is soft? Which is smooth and hard? Ask an adult first, and wash your hands. On the way to school, spot a mynah or a pigeon: what is its outer covering? If you see a frog or a mudskipper, look and do not pick it up.

parts.title: This Fish Walks on LAND! Is It Really a Fish? (Part 2) | Animal Groups
parts.description:
It hops about on the mud at Sungei Buloh, but it has fins, scales and gills. Is the mudskipper really a fish? Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity: animal groups (amphibians, birds and fish).

In this part:
• Birds: beaks, wings, eggs and feathers (a penguin cannot fly. Is it a bird?)
• Fish: fins, scales and gills
• Be the mudskipper: the tide goes out and you hop onto the mud
• A starfish is not a fish

Key words: feathers, fins, scales, gills.
Watch Part 1 first! Next episode: Count the legs! Insects, reptiles and mammals.
